summary: A local community health center ran a series of wellness workshops starting September 5, 2023, on how wearables and health apps can help people manage their health. Experts covered data tracking, app features, data privacy, interpreting health metrics, food tracking and the future of digital health. Facilitators stressed balancing technology with in-person care and using these tools judiciously.
one_line: A community health center's fall 2023 workshop series taught residents to use wearables and health apps, covering privacy, metrics, nutrition and the future, while keeping traditional care.
key_facts: The local community health center's wellness workshops on technology in health began on September 5, 2023.
Dr. Angela Hartley and tech entrepreneur Jason Torres were keynote speakers on the opening day.
Dr. Hartley explained that wearables such as smartwatches or fitness bands collect data on steps, heart rate, sleep patterns and oxygen saturation.
Local teacher Claire Emerson credited her smartwatch with early detection of an irregular heartbeat, leading to a doctor visit and treatment.
On September 10, Jason Torres gave a live demonstration of integrating health data from various apps into a comprehensive health dashboard on a phone or computer.
Modern health apps can track nutritional intake, meditation sessions and cognitive health through brain-training exercises, and some use artificial intelligence for personalized advice.
Cyber security expert Nina Patel covered data privacy and security, including understanding privacy policies of wearables and consumer rights.
At the September 17 workshop, attendees voiced concerns about sharing health data with insurance companies and potential misuse of information.
Cardiologist Dr. Omar Jin's September 20 session covered interpreting heart rate variability and resting heart rate.
Nutritionist Lisa Nguyen's September 26 workshop showed how food tracking apps can help tailor diets, identify deficiencies and manage weight.
On October 1, futurist Mark Stevens envisioned wearables and apps predicting health concerns before they become significant.
Facilitators stressed balancing technology with traditional healthcare, since in-person consultation with professionals remains indispensable.
